purpose: Sagittal alignment family for the skeleton-first C2-S1 rebuild. Keeps source sign conventions explicit and avoids forcing one population mean into every individual.

C2_C7_lordosis_deg.source_sign: positive lordosis; therefore the mean is near neutral/slightly opposite in that convention

geometry_definitions.hip_axis: midpoint between left/right femoral head centres
geometry_definitions.pelvic_thickness: distance from hip axis to centre of S1 superior endplate
geometry_definitions.pelvic_tilt: angle of HA↔S1-centre line relative to vertical
geometry_definitions.sacral_slope: angle of S1 superior endplate relative to horizontal

cervical_segment_family.note: This source gives a visibly more lordotic mean than the Hasegawa male global average. Treat this as a legitimate normal-shape family/source conflict, not a value to average blindly.

lumbar_segment_family.relationship: Distal lordosis dominates; L5/S1 contributes the largest share. This pattern should be preserved even if the canonical total LL is selected nearer the male Hasegawa mean of 56.4°.

canonical_rules: Neutral standing alignment is not one rigid universal curve. The master stores a canonical reference pose plus evidence corridors.
Pelvic incidence is a morphological parameter; select PI/SS/PT coherently rather than setting lumbar lordosis independently.
For a typical reference male, the Hasegawa male PI (~50°), SS (~41°), thoracic kyphosis (~44°) and lumbar lordosis (~56°) form a mutually plausible global family.
Distribute lumbar lordosis distally, with L4/5 and L5/S1 carrying the majority, consistent with asymptomatic segmental data.
Cervical source conflict remains explicit. Do not force the sum of Reinhold segmental means onto the Hasegawa global male mean without choosing a reference posture/population and sign convention.
Every level orientation must be derived from endplate frames, not from rotating stretched a003 bone sticks.
Use PTh + PT to position the S1 superior-endplate centre from the retained hip axis; use SS to orient the S1 endplate. Keep these as a coherent geometric family rather than independent coordinates.
next_coordinate_solve: Choose a provisional canonical PI inside the male standing corridor and derive SS/PT consistently.
Choose the global L1-S1 lordosis within the male corridor and distribute it using the level pattern, then verify T12/L1 endplate angles.
Build T1-T12 kyphosis using the global male corridor plus rib/thoracic attachment constraints.
Choose the cervical reference family explicitly (near-neutral versus more lordotic normal family), then map C2-C7 endplate signs into HGPT coordinates.
Check global SVA/head-over-pelvis after the complete stack is reconstructed.
